newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to examine new beef label compromise.
newsitem.headline: EU to examine new beef label compromise.

text.p: European Union farm ministers are due on Wednesday to discuss a new compromise from the Dutch EU Presidency to try and break a deadlock over compulsory beef labelling, EU officials said.

Britain and Italy were resisting plans, aimed at reassuring consumers scared away from beef due to a health scare over mad cow disease, making it obligatory to state the origin of beef sold in shops from January 2000.
"The compromise was amended following a series of bilateral discussions," an EU official said.

Ministers must reach unanimous agreement after rejecting a new proposal from the European Commission to give the European Parliament joint decision-making power over a proposal to set up EU cattle identification and beef labelling systems.

The EU's executive revised its proposal, originally presented in October, in order to meet parliament's demands for more power and tougher controls and to avoid a possible vote of censure in November.
Under the Dutch compromise, the parliament would revert to its traditional advisory role.
Britain and Italy were resisting the fixing of a deadline for labelling on beef where the animal was born, raised and slaughtered, officials said.
Britain is worried that such information would scare off shoppers. It argues that obligatory labelling of the origin of beef would create a trade barrier in the single EU market.
Italy, which imports a lot of calves from eastern Europe for fattening, is concerned that putting such information on labels would create an adverse reaction among Italian consumers.
However officials said that exemptions might be granted so that the two countries did not need to label the origin of beef.
